title: Corporate web proxy no Kerberos auth for iframe content since 108.0.1
body: We use a corporate proxy with Kerberos authentication and a policy that allows no content without authentication. Since Firefox updated to 108.0.1, authentication is sent for the main page but not for embedded iframe content, so the proxy refuses the iframe connection. This persists across different laptops and virtual machines. Older Firefox versions work, but the issue returns after updating; Beta and Nightly are also affected. Nothing changed on our corporate proxy. The proxy logs show that no authentication is sent for the iframe request. I attached a screenshot.

symptoms_visible: The main page loads through our Kerberos-authenticated corporate proxy, but its embedded iframe is refused because Firefox sends no authentication for that request.
The problem appears on different laptops and virtual machines in Firefox 108.0.1, Beta, and Nightly; an older Firefox version loads the iframe normally.
N0.label: N0 iframe proxy authentication regression reported

symptoms_visible: The main page still loads, while the iframe request reaches the proxy without authentication and is refused.
N1.label: N1 mozregression output collected

symptoms_visible: The iframe content remains unavailable through the corporate proxy, while the rest of the page loads.
N2.label: N2 HTTP log delivered

symptoms_visible: I cannot find any X-Frame-Options setting to disable on the proxy, and the iframe is still refused while the main page loads.
N2_x.label: N2_x proxy-header workaround rejected

symptoms_visible: In today's Nightly build, the page and its embedded iframe load without any issues through the corporate proxy.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved in Nightly

question_patterns: Could you run mozregression to determine which Firefox change introduced the problem?
Can you bisect the regression between an older working Firefox build and the affected build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran mozregression. It reported a 2022-11-11 Firefox 108.0a1 build with changeset b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789 and this pushlog: https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/pushloghtml?fromchange=df541ee6f62267803ead2b4e966dc2c06a23c58a&tochange=b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My run shows the iframe already failing in every older build I tested, so mozregression could not produce a Firefox regression range.
I obtained the same pushlog range from a second mozregression run using slightly different good and bad starting builds.

edges.comment: From c1-c2 on the reporter's system: the reporter ran mozregression and pasted its raw build metadata, changeset, and pushlog URL. Mapping that range to the regressing networking change is engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: Could you record an HTTP log while reproducing the failed iframe request and send it privately?
Please capture Firefox networking logs for one reproduction and share them through the requested private channel.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded the HTTP log and sent the file to you by email.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I captured the problem, but the log contains no iframe request or proxy response at all.
I sent the same HTTP log as a compressed file instead of an uncompressed file.

edges.comment: From c3-c5 on the reporter's system: the reporter privately emailed the requested HTTP log. The X-Frame-Options line and its interpretation were produced later by engineers and are not leaked through the user's answer.

solution.intent: Treat the X-Frame-Options response as a corporate-proxy configuration problem and temporarily disable that header on the proxy.
solution.concrete_example: The HTTP log contains an X-Frame-Options: deny response, so confirm whether the proxy adds it and try disabling that header on the proxy as a temporary workaround.
solution.inference_hint: The X-Frame-Options line was read by an engineer from the privately supplied HTTP log; the reporter only said that the file was emailed.

edges.comment: From c9-c11 on the reporter's deployment: an engineer suspected that the proxy added X-Frame-Options: deny and suggested disabling it. The reporter rejected this direction with configuration evidence: no such option was available, the proxy did not manipulate website content, and the response was believed to be the proxy's unauthenticated fallback after Firefox omitted Kerberos.

solution.intent: Back out the regressing iframe authentication-suppression behavior so an unauthenticated proxy response carrying X-Frame-Options or CSP restrictions does not prevent Firefox from performing proxy authentication, then have the reporter verify a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: Back out the change that suppresses authentication for iframe requests judged unframeable from an X-Frame-Options or CSP response. Then ask the reporter to retest today's Nightly and confirm whether both the page and iframe load through the Kerberos-authenticated proxy.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers mapped the raw mozregression range to the change that disabled authentication handling for iframe requests expected to fail framing checks. Combining that change with the private log showed that an unauthenticated proxy response containing X-Frame-Options: deny caused Firefox to suppress the Kerberos authentication flow. The reporter supplied the range, log, and proxy observations but did not derive this mechanism.

edges.comment: From c12-c24: maintainers backed out the regressing behavior, landed it, and the same reporter installed the following day's Nightly and confirmed that the page loaded without issues. Later uplift and release-note coordination is deliberately unscored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final root cause: Firefox's iframe framing guard treated an unauthenticated proxy response carrying X-Frame-Options or CSP restrictions as proof that the iframe could not load and suppressed the proxy authentication flow, so Kerberos was never sent.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the older-build comparison, raw mozregression range, private HTTP log, and the reporter's explanation of the proxy's unauthenticated fallback response.
Must recommend backing out or removing the regressing iframe authentication-suppression behavior so proxy authentication can complete for iframe requests.
Must not settle on disabling X-Frame-Options at the corporate proxy: the reporter had no such option, stated that the proxy did not manipulate website content, and the direction was inapplicable.

Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the fix and only treat the issue as resolved after the reporter confirms that the page and iframe load; the reporter did confirm this in the following day's Nightly.

persona_hint.experience_level: Enterprise IT user familiar with corporate Kerberos proxies and proxy logs; able to install older, Beta, and Nightly builds, run mozregression, and privately capture HTTP logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise, with informal wording and occasional spelling errors; provides requested diagnostics promptly and challenges configuration assumptions using knowledge of the corporate proxy.
